name: reviewing-scientific-literature

# Reviewing Scientific Literature


## Procedure
1. Define a focused question, review type, search period, disciplines and inclusion/exclusion rules. Distinguish a targeted research scan from a systematic review; do not claim exhaustive coverage without a reproducible search/screening process.
2. Search appropriate scholarly sources available in the environment. Save exact query, provider, filters, date and results. Verify title/authors/year/DOI against the paper or publisher. Record inaccessible full texts; do not infer full methods from abstracts.
3. Deduplicate preprints/journal versions by identifiers and content. Record version, corrections or retractions if known. Treat preprints as such, not as peer-reviewed by default.
4. Extract task, population, data provenance/license, target definition, independent n, split design, baseline, metrics, uncertainty, compute, code and limitations. Identify entity/temporal leakage and incompatible benchmarks.
5. Build an evidence matrix with supported claim and exact section/page/table locator. Separate author claims from independently checked facts and your interpretation. Use short necessary quotations or faithful paraphrases, respecting source limits.
6. Synthesize agreement, disagreement, bias and evidence gaps. Do not pool incompatible outcomes; meta-analysis requires comparable estimands, dependence handling and heterogeneity assessment.
7. For systematic reviews use applicable PRISMA reporting guidance and report flow/exclusions; it is a reporting framework, not proof of study quality. For scoping reviews use the appropriate extension.
## Deliver
Write `search-log.csv`, `evidence-matrix.csv`, verified `references.bib` and `literature-synthesis.md`. Propose specific next experiments, not unsupported novelty claims.
## Stop or hand off
Missing full text is marked unverified. Never invent a DOI, effect estimate, citation or paper. Pass empirical plans to the experiment and modeling skills.
